subject: Operational signal: wins, blockers, QBR prep (week of 2027-06-20)
body:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
Cc: EngOps (Acme Analytics) <engops@acme-analytics.com>, Morgan Patel <morgan@venturecap.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Operational signal: wins, blockers, QBR prep (week of 2027-06-20)

Good morning all —

Quick weekly signal from Platform Ops ahead of QBR prep. Short bullets for wins, tight risks, and specific asks we need to lock before the pack deadline next Thursday. I attached the current QBR playbook and a sensitivity sheet for the Dedicated bookings projection.

Wins:
- Hosted API latency  p50 down to 42ms (global) after kernel selection changes — customer-facing benchmarks will go into the QBR appendix.
- Closed POC with Acme Analytics; initial Dedicated commit (2x A100 pools) now scheduled for July (deal HS-98765). EngOps on thread to coordinate onboarding.
- Completed rollout of prefix-KV caching in region-eu which reduced token cost by ~8% on our top-10 routes.

Risks / Tight items:
- Capacity: Dedicated pool provisioning timeline is 6–8 business days. If Acme wants an early ramp (mid-July), we need expedited bare-metal slots from infra — ask to Infra (Jonas) below.
- Quality regression: a small prompt-set shows increased hallucination on long-form summaries after quantization switch. We have a canary but need a decision on rollback vs. micro-tune before QBR.
- QBR narrative: we have strong economics but need a single chart that maps unit token cost vs. latency across top 5 customers — data team needs around 48 hours to consolidate.

Asks (action owners & deadlines):
- Jonas: confirm the expedited provisioning option (can we shave 3 days?) and estimate any incremental cost. Deadline: Tue 2027-06-22 5pm PT.
- Maya: lead the quality action (micro-tune vs rollback) — propose a path in <24h and prepare a short slide showing tradeoffs for the QBR appendix. Deadline: Mon 2027-06-21 noon PT.
- Laura: finalize the customer narrative and pick the three customer stories for the ‘reliability’ slide. I recommend Acme (new commit), BetaBank (latency win), and VentureCap pilot. Deadline: Wed 2027-06-23 EOD.
- EngOps (Acme): confirm onboarding calendar and the contact for network/KMS handoff.

Attachments: QBR_playbook_v3.pdf (master deck + slide templates), cost-sensitivity-sheet.xlsx (Dedicated revenue scenarios).

I’ll collect inputs and produce a one-pager for the exec slide reviewers on Thursday morning.

Thanks,
Lukas Meyer
Director, Platform Ops
Redwood Inference

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational signal: wins, blockers, QBR prep (week of 2027-06-20)

Thanks, Lukas — good concise layout. Two quick additions:

- I’ll make the case narrative concise: 1 slide (problem/opportunity), 1 slide (evidence: metrics + customer quotes), 1 slide (ask/ask size).
- For customer stories, add a short quote from the BetaBank CS lead — I’ll pull that and drop into the drive doc tonight.

Acking Jonas & Maya for their parts.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
VP, GTM Strategy
Redwood Inference

---

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational signal: wins, blockers, QBR prep (week of 2027-06-20)

On provisioning — short update: we can prioritize two racks in the pool for Acme and target a T-3 day on provisioning if we reassign an in-flight procurement batch (there is a ~$12k one-time expedite fee and minor risk to the next small-batch customer slot).

Options:
1) Standard schedule (6–8 business days) — no incremental cost.
2) Expedite (target T-3 days) — pay expedite fee, slight risk to next customer slot.

I recommend option 2 for Acme given revenue and PR value — will stand up a blunt ETA once we have final approval.

Jonas Weber
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

---

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jun 2027 12:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational signal: wins, blockers, QBR prep (week of 2027-06-20)

I ran the micro-tune test overnight and have preliminary numbers: the model recovers precision on long-form summaries at the cost of a 4% latency increase (p95). I’ll produce a 90-second demo and a one-slide before noon PT showing: baseline vs micro-tuned vs rollback (numbers + short guidance).

If we lean rollback, it buys latency but loses the improved cost profile from the new quantization; if we micro-tune we keep cost gains but accept a small latency hit. My recommendation will be micro-tune + targeted prompt-adjustments for the three affected customers.

Maya Srinivasan
Head of Applied ML
Redwood Inference

---

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>, EngOps (Acme Analytics) <engops@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jun 2027 16:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational signal: wins, blockers, QBR prep (week of 2027-06-20)

Thanks all — plan below and next steps:
- Jonas: proceed with expedite (option 2). Please confirm procurement ticket and estimated ship date by EOD Tue.
- Maya: finalize micro-tune slide + 90s demo by Wed 11am PT. We will present micro-tune and fallback plan in the QBR appendix.
- Laura: consolidate the three customer stories and drop the one-pager in the Drive link by Wed EOD.
- EngOps (Acme): please share the preferred onboarding date window (Jul 11–15 or Jul 18–22) and your KMS contact.

I’ll compile the exec one-pager and circulate to the reviewers by Thu 07:00 PT.

Lukas

Attachments: QBR_playbook_v3.pdf, cost-sensitivity-sheet.xlsx
